# The examples open on a groups overview, and every group stays in reach

> **Corrected Mon 16 Nov 2026, the day it was filed.** This ticket went up without Discussion #20742, which holds the same capacity measurement (eight labels, 11 Nov), the operator's recorded preference for a groups overview with a breadcrumb sibling switcher, and my own two reads there. The inventory on #20498 then changed the premise ([map v2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20498#issuecomment-6918253093)): the section gets 22 groups in four bands, not ten tabs. The measurement below stands. The candidates, the first three criteria and the title are replaced; the old title was "The examples navigation shows every family without a menu", and its criterion excluded the operator's preference before any frame existed.

`[PROVISIONAL_UNGRADUATED: D#20742]` The navigation is OQ3 of Discussion #20742 and has not graduated. The group list, its OQ1, was bound by the operator on 16 Nov 2026 and is written out on #21141 with ids, paths and each record's home group. Until OQ3 graduates, or the operator rules, the desktop control of a group page stays open (the upright list or the breadcrumb switcher). **Direction taken on 17 Nov 2026 under Nightshift** ([the second pass](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21130#issuecomment-6936132087)): the build may start with what both options share (the overview, the banded index as one component, the counts, and on the phone the crumb with its full-list sheet), toward the pick of the design seat, the upright list on the desktop. The operator reads the pair at the merge gate of the build, and an objection there or a different marking of OQ3 changes the desktop control only. The Fix, the Contract Ledger and the Acceptance Criteria were refreshed on 17 Nov for the phased build, after the OQ3 disposition on the Discussion ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/20742#discussioncomment-19668684)); the desktop control of phase 2 stays `[OQ_RESOLUTION_PENDING]`.

| Option | When this would be right | Falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| Overview page, breadcrumb with a sibling switcher (the operator's recorded preference, and the recommendation until a first-click read says otherwise: I conceded on the Discussion on 11 Nov that his preference decides where no unprimed reader is available) | Readers open the switcher unprompted, and the cards keep their width. | A first-click read: from one group, reach another. The switcher needs a hint. |
| Overview page, upright group list beside the cards | Readers want the whole list in view while they tick through groups. | The list costs card width: a family card falls under the scale at which cover text reads (0.64, #21121). |
| Today's rotated rail with its overflow control | The section stays at five tabs. | Map v2 has 22 groups; three show at 1280×720 today. |

**The first-click read of 17 Nov:** both new controls were found without a hint, so the switcher's falsifier did not trigger; today's rail failed. The list's falsifier is live at 1440×900: the sketch's frame shows three columns of 366 px there, cover text at about 0.57, so the list needs the two-column rule of phase 2 to stay above 0.64.

## Context

On 16 Nov 2026 the examples section's rail was measured while its first screen was read for covers (headless Chromium against the branch of #21124). The rail is the left tab bar every Portal section shares. #20690 moved the example families into it and put the build control at its foot. Five tabs publish on `dev`. #21129 adds Scheduler, Gantt and Board, and Components and State & Data publish with their first covered record (#21120, #20696).

A leaf of #20498, cornerstone 1 of Engine 14 (`ROADMAP.md`), cut on Mon 23 Nov.

## The Problem

A rotated tab needs its label's width plus 46 px (font `600 16px Source Sans 3`; the constant is 45.6 to 46.3 px across the five rendered tabs).

| Tab | Height | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Featured | 107 px | measured |
| Grid & Table | 129 px | measured |
| Forms | 89 px | measured |
| Multi-Window | 142 px | measured |
| Calendar | 108 px | measured |
| Scheduler | 115 px | from the same font metrics |
| Gantt | 84 px | from the same font metrics |
| Board | 87 px | from the same font metrics |
| Components | 134 px | from the same font metrics |
| State & Data | 130 px | from the same font metrics |
| The build control | 156 px | measured |

Ten tabs need 1,125 px, with the build control 1,281 px. The rail is the viewport's height minus the 58 px header:

| Viewport | Rail | Families shown of ten |
|---|---:|---|
| 1920×1080 | 1,022 px | 7 (computed) |
| 1440×900 | 842 px | 5 (computed) |
| 1366×768 | 710 px | 4 (computed) |
| 1280×720 | 662 px | 3 (observed today with five families: Multi-Window and Calendar sit behind the overflow control) |

The computed rows reserve the build control and 48 px for the overflow control, the size read off the 1280×720 frame. No row sits within 39 px of a threshold.

At 1280×720 a stranger reads Featured, Grid & Table, Forms and a three-dot button. Nothing says that Calendar, Scheduler, Gantt, Board, Multi-Window, Components or State & Data exist. `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` keeps the active tab visible, so a visitor who lands on `/examples/gantt` sees Gantt and loses another family instead.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/portal/view/shared/TabContainer.mjs`: `tabBarPosition: 'left'` and `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` on the header toolbar, for News and Examples (#20599).
- `apps/portal/view/examples/TabContainer.mjs`: `familyDefinitions` is the one ordered source of family, title, route and icon; `buildModes` feed the control at the rail's foot (`'Build: ' + …`, #20690).
- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`: headers beyond the bar's main-axis extent collapse behind one control; the active and the focused header are protected.
- Styles: `resources/scss/src/apps/portal/shared/TabContainer.scss`, `resources/scss/src/apps/portal/examples/List.scss`.
- Design authority: "One overview page per family on the portal at the kitchen-sink standard" (#20498, Intended solution shape 1). The rail's capacity was never decided. #20690 kept "the section's tab bar" as an avoided trap of that leaf, and #20599 put "the bar's visual design: rotated labels, icons" out of scope while noting that "each new tab still costs height".

## The Fix

The looks are posted: [the first look](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21130#issuecomment-6918809237) and [the second pass](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21130#issuecomment-6936132087), with their boards and cold reads. The build runs in two phases, and phase 1 binds no desktop control.

1. **Phase 1, what both controls share** (may start now):
   - **The overview at `/examples`:** the groups in the four bands of #21141, three group cards above a banded index, the counts, and `sentence` and `tile` per group, as on the revised board. Where the Featured selection stands follows the board.
   - **The banded index as one component** with three presentations: the overview's index, the desktop control of a group page (phase 2) and the phone's sheet. `familyDefinitions` stays its one source.
   - **The phone, below 640 px:** a group page keeps the crumb, and its group button opens the full list in its four bands as a sheet. One tap opens the sheet, a second navigates. There is no strip that scrolls.
   - **Counts** as the second pass says under "For the build": home records only, a cross-listed record is shown and not counted, and a group without a card shows no entry.
2. **Phase 2, the desktop control of a group page**, the last and smallest step. `[OQ_RESOLUTION_PENDING]`: it is OQ3 of Discussion #20742.
   - **C, the upright list** (the design seat's pick): the index stands beside the cards and ends above the fold at 720 px. Beside the list the cards keep two columns until a third leaves each card 410 px or wider, so that cover text arrives at 0.64 of its size (#21121): a viewport of about 1,570 px.
   - **B, the breadcrumb's sibling switcher** (the operator's recorded preference): the pill says how many groups it holds and does not look like the build control, and a link to the next group ends the cards. The breadcrumb and route constraints of Discussion #20742 (its "Source constraints" section and Julia's comment) are part of that build.
   - The operator reads the pair at this pull request's merge gate. That read is OQ3's ruling and is recorded on the Discussion, not only on the pull request.
3. News and Learn keep the shared rail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The looks are on this ticket: the front door and three group-page candidates with the groups of map v2 at 1440×900, 1280×720 and 390×844, beside the released page, with cold reads (16 and 17 Nov).
- [ ] On `/examples` every published group is visible by name at 1440×900, 1366×768 and 1280×720, by scrolling at most one screen and without opening a menu.
- [ ] From a group page every other group is reached in at most two actions, and two readers without session context find the way unprompted.
- [ ] At 390×844 and 390×664 every published group is on the overview by name, by scrolling at most one screen. On a group page one tap opens the full list and a second navigates. No strip that scrolls.
- [ ] The build control stays one control, takes no space a group needs, and the four build routes resolve as before.
- [ ] Keyboard and focus: the index is a navigation landmark whose entries are links. Tab reaches it and every entry, Enter navigates, and the active group carries `aria-current="page"`. The sheet (and the switcher's menu, if B binds) takes focus when it opens, closes on Escape, returns focus to its button, and its button exposes whether it is open. No entry claims to be a selected tab.
- [ ] A group without a covered member shows no entry (#21124, #21141), and its route opens `/examples`.
- [ ] What the static boards do not show is proven in the build: direct entry on a group route, browser history, one writer of the route, the selected build mode kept across groups, the scroll position per group, and counts that follow the records the build mode publishes.
- [ ] If C binds: beside the list no family card is narrower than 410 px.
- [ ] An e2e arm drives the published groups at 1280×720 and the sheet at 390×844. It fails on today's rail.
- [ ] **Look:** the pull request shows the whole section as released and as changed at the three sizes, and two readers without session context grade the unlabelled pair. The operator's read of the desktop pair is recorded on Discussion #20742 as OQ3's ruling.
- [ ] News and Learn render their rail as before.

## Out of Scope

The cards and covers (#21124, #20679, #21120, #21121); which families exist (#21129, the map on #20498); the rail of News and Learn; a search field or grouping inside a family; what a family with one example shows on its page.

## Avoided Traps

- **Moving the build control only.** It returns 156 px, one family.
- **Shorter labels or icons only.** #20599 named it: each new tab still costs height.
- **One tab for Calendar, Scheduler, Gantt and Board.** Their routes are separate search landings (#21116).
- **A new navigation for every Portal section.** The measurement is the examples' ten families; News has seven tabs and its overflow control was the answer there.
- **Deciding the navigation from the day's tab count.** Ten tabs were the count of 16 Nov; the map has 22 groups, and the next one is a line in `familyDefinitions`.
- **Scrolling the rotated rail.** #20599 rejected it: a scroll without an affordance leaves hidden tabs undiscovered.

The sketches are that overview with covers, counts and the applications.

**Cold look.** Two readers without session context, unlabelled frames in different orders, desktop and phone, each first screen graded 1 to 10 (informed, excited, convinced):

| First screen | An engineer evaluating UI platforms | An AI agent checking seven needs for its user |
|---|---:|---:|
| Released 13.4 | 3 | 2 |
| Today on `dev` | 5 | 5 |
| Overview, applications first | 7 | 7 |
| Overview, groups first | 6 | 8 |

- Today's page, the engineer: "there is no headline or count, so I can't tell whether the catalog is 6 items or 600". The agent confirmed two of its seven needs from it, and all seven from either overview.
- The engineer ranks applications first (scope, proof and specifics on one screen). The agent ranks groups first (all eleven groups above the fold; on the phone six groups against four).
- Limits: both readers ran from this checkout and the frames show the product's name; the sketches are static; one frame per state and size.

**What keeps it from a 9, named by both readers**

1. Proof and scope belong on the same screen: every group above the fold, and the applications in view. One anchor for the eye, not eleven equal tiles.
2. The tiles are texture. Small, light and dark mixed, and several read as toys (a lorem-ipsum tree, a cube, a clock, an empty calendar). Each needs a cover that shows its one feature at a readable size, in one theme.
3. The numbers do not reconcile: "150" against 79 that can be counted, and "curated" where a number should stand.
4. "Build: Production" is unexplained in the best place of the page.
5. No action that tests the claim ("open the 100,000 × 200 grid"), and no cue that a card opens live (#21131).
6. The thin groups show: Scheduler 1, Gantt 1, Calendar 2.
7. Phone: the groups have to be in reach within the first 844 px, and the applications row needs a cue that it scrolls.

The engineer's first point is larger than this page: nothing on it says what Neo.mjs is.

**Next (mine, Tue 17 Nov):** a second pass with points 1 to 5 and 7 folded, and the group page three ways (the prototype's switcher scaled to 22 groups, an upright list, today's rail), read by first click. The group list was bound on 16 Nov (#21141); the navigation's build waits for the pick.

Rendered on `dev` `a442f37f3e` with the 22 groups of #21162. The overview and the two new group-page controls are static markup laid over the running Portal; the cards on the group pages are the real ones. Nothing is built.

**Cold look at the overview.** Readers without session context, unlabelled frames at 1280×720 and 390×844 in different orders, each first screen graded 1 to 10.

| First screen | An engineer, first read | A second engineer | An AI agent checking seven needs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Released 13.4 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Today on `dev` | 5 | 5 | 4 |
| Second pass, first composition | 7 | not shown | not shown |
| Second pass, revised | not shown | 8 | 8 |

- **The first read moved the layout.** The first composition (one anchor, a text index of every group) informed and did not excite: informed 9, excited 5, convinced 7. Today's page is the reverse: informed 4, excited 7. The reader's first wish was thumbnails in the card style of today's page above the fold, and a shorter introduction that leads with the claim.
- **The revision** puts three group cards above the index, leads with "Grids with 100,000 rows × 200 columns" and makes the action that claim's test ("Open the 100,000 × 200 grid"). The second engineer read it at 8 (informed 9, excited 7, convinced 7).
- **Folded from the second read, shown on the board and not read again by an engineer:** one line on what Neo.mjs is, Forms & Fields among the three cards, and on the phone every group by name on the first screen in place of a row of cards. Both engineers tried to add up the counts, so a cross-list now stands in parentheses.
- **The AI agent read the folded version at 8** and confirmed all seven of its needs from the first screen, five firmly and two softly (the word "validation" is nowhere, and "(3)" is unexplained). From today's page it confirmed one, from the released page none.
- **What keeps it from a 9 is evidence, in both personas' words: told, not shown.** The cards and tiles need covers that show the claim: a grid with its locked columns and an edited cell, and a calendar, a scheduler, a Gantt chart and a chart that can be seen. The tree example shows lorem ipsum. That is #21146, #21120, #21121 and the slate (#21142), not this layout.

**First click on a group page.** Task from Grid & Table: reach the Calendar examples, and say which other groups exist. Each reader answered cold on one candidate and then saw the other two.

| | Reader 1, cold on B (the switcher) | Reader 2, cold on C (the list) |
|---|---|---|
| Cold answer | clicks the "Grid & Table ▾" pill and expects a list of groups: 2 clicks, confidence 4, corrected to 3 after seeing the list. Cannot tell from the screen which groups exist | clicks "Calendar" in the list: 1 click, confidence 5. Reads the groups off the screen, confidence 4: the list's last row touches the edge at 720 px |
| A, today's rail | Calendar is not on the rail at 1280×720: "···" and hope, 2 clicks, confidence 3 | the same: 2 to 3 clicks, confidence 2 |
| B, the switcher | cold, above | the pill, 2 clicks, confidence 4; which groups exist is not on screen, confidence 3 |
| C, the upright list | 1 click, confidence 5; every group visible with its count | cold, above |
| Phone | B: the pill, 2 taps, confidence 4. C's strip: Calendar is clipped, confidence 3 | C's strip: Calendar is not visible, swipe and tap, confidence 3. B: the pill, 2 taps, confidence 4 |
| Pick | C: reach and scope | B: the same two clicks at both sizes, and half again as many cards |

**The readers split, and each picked the candidate they had not met first. My pick as the design seat: C on the desktop, and on the phone B's crumb, whose group button opens the full list.**

- **Both new controls work without a hint; today's rail does not.** Both readers found the pill and the list unprompted. On the rail neither could find Calendar at 1280×720 (confidence 2 and 3).
- **The switcher loses on the second question.** Nothing on a group page says which groups exist until the menu is open (confidence 2 and 3 against 4 and 5), and the pill repeats the page's heading, so it reads as a label.
- **The list's price is one column of cards, under a rule the 1440 frame does not apply.** At 1280×720 the frames show two columns beside the list and three under the switcher: four cards on the first screen against six. Each card is wider, so its cover text arrives at 0.77 of its size against 0.60. At 1440×900 the list's frame shows three columns of 366 px, cover text at about 0.57, under the 0.64 measure of #21121: the sketch let the card grid fill (`minmax(340px, 1fr)`). By the same rule the switcher has three columns of about 455 px there (computed, about 0.68). * feat(themes): convert the theme sources to plain CSS with a proving converter (#21217)

buildScripts/helpers/convertScssToCss.mjs writes resources/css from resources/scss and
compiles both to prove each pair equal. At 825047c9ea: 722 of 722 files identical; 720
converted, 2 compiled (D4), 15 flattened in place (D2/D3), the D3 negative control (Euclid's
shorthand falsifier, #18182 comment 19670346) passing. Flattening replaces lifting single
rules, which reordered them against their siblings (#18182 comment 19670216).

Beyond the Discussion's rules, the compiled files keep their comments, adjacent line
comments become one block, and each block that Sass shared and the conversion copies
names its other copies.

Equality under Sass cannot see where Sass reads more leniently than a browser, so every
declaration value is also probed through Sass and Sass's reading is adopted where it differs
(custom properties and CSS math functions exempt). One case on this tree: the trailing comma
in Range's `input[type=range]::-moz-range-track,` selector, which Sass drops and a browser
rejects with the whole rule.

The build still compiles resources/scss until the next commit.

build-themes and watch-themes read resources/css. Every .css file is a class sheet, copied

watcher's partial freshness boundaries, root-forced rebuilds and Sass preload go.

- list, the default and the design seat's pick: the banded index stands
  upright beside the heading and the cards, and ends above the fold of a
  720 px viewport (at 693 px for 1280x720).
- switcher, the operator's recorded preference: the crumb shows at every
  width, its group button is a pill naming how many groups the selected
  build publishes, and a link to the next group ends the cards (GroupIndex
  presentation next; after the last group it leads to the overview).

Below 640 px both keep the crumb's sheet. No card is narrower than 410 px:
two columns of 562 px beside the index at 1440x900, three of about 450 px
with the switcher.

The page places its five items on a CSS grid instead of nesting them, so the
cards stay a direct child of the page that scrolls, the root of their
intersection observer. Its rows are max-content: with auto rows the
overflowing page left no free space, and the header, which clips, shrank to
its padding under the cards. List#onIntersect now returns for a record that
a build switch dropped (a TypeError in the App Worker during the counts arm).

The config and the control the ruling does not pick leave the pull request
with that ruling.

The Look of #21241 at 1440x900, 1280x720 and 390x844: neomjs.com as a
visitor's browser shows it (dark theme), and this branch with the upright
index and with the switcher. The next commit drops them; the pull request
links them at this commit.

* docs(portal): drop the review frames; they stay at ae1bf69d2f (#21130)

* test(portal): the news bar proves its overflow control on its own (#21130)

The desktop arm of NewsTabOverflow used the examples tab bar as the
bar that does not fit at 1920 px; this branch replaces that bar with
the overview. The News bar now shows both states itself (1920 × 800
keeps the control, 1920 × 1080 withdraws it), and leaving News for
Examples takes the control along.

* feat(portal): the list is the one desktop control, and its index scrolls on its own (#21130)

OQ3 is settled on Discussion #20742: the list. The switcher, its pill,
the next-group link and `groupControl` leave, and with them the
GroupIndex `next` presentation and the switcher's CSS and specs.

The upright index already scrolled on its own, but its padding sat
outside `max-height`, so at 16 groups its box ran 32 px past a 720 px
viewport. It now sizes as `border-box`. The list arm checks the box
against the viewport and scrolls the index to its last group, instead
of requiring every group above the fold, which the target's 21 groups
cannot meet at 1280x720.
